commit.message:
docs: reconcile the public record with the published state

The README and PUBLICATION-METADATA.yaml still described this record as
PRIVATE/LOCAL — NOT PUBLISHED, with the tag NOT CREATED and no release
performed. The repository is public, the signed tag exists, the release was
published on 2026-08-22 and the archive is deposited at Zenodo under
10.5281/zenodo.22056151. The landing surface contradicted the release it sits
on top of.

Correct both to current truth and record the published identity exactly: Git
commit and tree, the signed tag object, the archive and detached freeze record
with their byte counts and SHA-256s, the root-manifest identity, and both the
version and concept DOIs. Add the DOIs, version and release date to
CITATION.cff.

MANIFEST.sha256 is deliberately not regenerated. Its own SHA-256 is the
externally pinned root-manifest identity cited by the deposited freeze record;
regenerating it would silently retire an identity external records already
cite. PUBLICATION-STATE-001.md instead records exactly which three
documentation files now diverge from it, with the frozen and current digest of
each, so the divergence is auditable rather than absorbed.

No evidence byte moved: 64 of the 67 manifest entries are unchanged, the
fifteen frozen identities are untouched, and the published archive still
verifies PASS against the pinned root manifest. No claim changed and no
non-claim was weakened. The terminal result remains Branch A — Explicit Bridge
Required.
